overall: The AG found the Malden Youth Council violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to post notice of its April 23 summit on the city website and by failing to approve minutes timely, but found no unlawful texting among a quorum.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Youth Council failed to post notice of its meetings, including an April 23 summit whose notice was only posted at local high schools.
allegations.key_passage: Nothing within the Open Meeting Law limits the notice requirement to those topics that will be subject to a vote.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Youth Council failed to create and approve minutes of its meetings in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Because minutes of these open meetings were not approved in a timely manner, we find that the Youth Council violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged members of the Youth Council were messaging each other, forming a quorum outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As we have been presented with no text message sent by a member of the Youth Council and reaching a quorum of the Youth Council, we find no violation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements
remedy_passage: We order the Youth Council’s immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
